name: EWWF Surrender, 16 April 2002

date.source: the fed's own subject line and broadcast text

matches.finish: Tom Collins pinned Ashlyn Summers with a powerbomb onto the handle of her own baseball bat, after Tommy Kain's ringside interference broke up her advantage.
Challenger Thomas Casey rolled up champion Smoove for the pin after Larry Gionet ran in from the crowd and blindsided Smoove, winning the title.
Ryan Sanders pinned Simon Solkoff with a Pedigree after Tommy Kain ran in and hit Solkoff with a Partycrasher DVD, honoring a deal with owner Adam Mitchell for a future shot at Tom Collins.
Jimmy Slade rolled up Axel Reed for the pin while holding Reed's own tights and the ropes.

matches.stipulation: EWWF Extreme Championship, parking-lot ladder match
matches.finish: Despair retrieved the championship from atop the ladder after a debuting Larry Spikowski ambushed and choked Randy Love unconscious with the Louisville Strangler and carried him off, revealed as Adam Mitchell's own recruit.

notes: Fully structured. Bronson Johnson was billed against Tommy Kain for the Junior Heavyweight/Cruiserweight title but never appeared; no match occurred. Grant Morrison (deceased, storyline) and Heather Morrison are referenced/appear only in a non-match backstage scene and are not yet minted.

name: EWWF Redemption

date.source: posting dates (5-6 June 2002); no exact show date is stated in the text

matches.finish: Solkoff pinned a mystery opponent named by owner Adam Mitchell -- former EWWF wrestler Jack Mannon -- with a sunset flip into a powerbomb (Shockwave).
David Rheaume, revealed as the mystery partner, pinned Dallas Winston with High Tymes; The Outpatients (Pyro and Manson) then turned on Winston until Jack Paine made the save.
Summers made Sanders submit to Sanders' own finisher, "It's Over".

matches.stipulation: EWWF United States Championship, Three Way King of the Hill (scaffold) match
matches.finish: Slade pinned Paine first (chair-assisted by Reed), then Reed pinned Slade for the title after Larry Gionet's ringside interference.

matches.stipulation: EWWF United States Championship, mandated immediate rematch
matches.finish: Owner Adam Mitchell ordered an instant rematch; Slade ambushed Reed and pinned him while holding the tights to regain the title.
Matthews hit Hagan with a smuggled wrench, then a frog splash, for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Surrender Extreme Championship, weapons brawl in a junkyard
matches.finish: Despair pinned Kontani with a Flying Frankensteiner after a chaotic weapons brawl among burning cars, retaining the title.

notes: The advertised Randy Love vs. Larry Spikowski cage match is not shown in the surviving broadcast text (a mock production-outage gag skips straight to the next segment); billed only, no result recorded.

name: EWWF Surrender, 17 July 2002

matches.finish: Slade retained, powerbombing Krumm with his feet on the ropes for the pin.
Camarelli pinned Thomas with a top-rope elbow. Afterward Jack Mannon and State of Emergency beat down the winners and formed the unit Freedom's Darkness.
Kain hit a Springboard Bulldog for the pin.
Owner Adam Mitchell declared the match a no-contest after both teams' "dream partner" eligibility ran out, mid-match; no winner.

matches.stipulation: Surrender Extreme Championship, "Brooklyn Bum Brawl" dumpster match
matches.finish: The Trinity's Simon Underwood and Junya Kontani ambushed champion Homeless Joe Boxcar, sealed him in the winning dumpster, and placed the unconscious Despair to be declared the winner and new champion.
The broadcast ran out of time amid three-way interference from The Trinity and the Riot Squad; no decision was rendered.

notes: Ryan Sanders' earlier interference costing Despair the Extreme Championship to Homeless Joe Boxcar is shown only in a recap clip of an undocumented, unheld prior card ("last week"); recorded on the title's own reign history from this clip, not served as its own show.

name: EWWF Surrender, 30 July 2002

matches.stipulation: handicap ambush, opened as a match under protest
matches.finish: Despair and Underwood battered a bloodied Solkoff with a tire iron until Homeless Joe Boxcar ran in to save him; both attackers fled and no decision was rendered.
After a first three-count was overturned for a shoulder up, Love won it clean moments later with a sunset flip rollup; Slade retaliated post-match by powerbombing Love through the announce table.

notes: Trevor Saladin cuts a post-match promo demanding the next United States Championship shot.

name: EWWF Surrender, 8 August 2002

matches.finish: Debuting Ragnarok pinned Sanders with Sanders' own finisher, "It's Over".

matches.stipulation: EWWF United States Championship (Spikowski defending in place of the injured champion, Randy Love)
matches.finish: Slade pinned Spikowski with his feet on the ropes to take the title; Saladin then made off with the physical belt.
Summers retained after Rheaume's own manager Lo Mein accidentally sprayed him with a fire extinguisher, dropping him into her pinning position.
Lo Mein hit a top-rope German suplex with a roll-up for the pin.
Camarelli clotheslined Paine into a Cepacelli rollup for the pin; Ash then ran in and attacked both losers.
Dunsk deliberately knocked himself out with his own fishbowl to frame Kain, winning by disqualification and ending Kain's win streak.
Demola reversed an inside cradle for the pin; Liam Zen then choked him out post-match.
Despair abandoned the match; A-Train pinned Underwood after a Syko/A-Train double move, giving the debuting Riot Squad the win.

notes: Closes with Simon Solkoff (EWWF World Champion) branding and burning himself in retaliation against a bound Despair and Underwood, building to the Kingdom of the Wicked pay-per-view.

name: EWWF Kingdom of the Wicked

date.source: the fed's own subject lines across all six served parts

matches.stipulation: Surrender Extreme Championship (the card's own commentary also calls this the Sex Championship and states outright it is the same belt)
matches.finish: Ashlyn Summers retained after a chaotic tables-ladders-and-chairs brawl that included a near-loss off a back drop driver through a table, finally pinning a recovering Homeless Joe Boxcar with a second attempt at lifting him into the ring.
Evil Badman rolled up A-Train with his feet on the ropes for a fast three-count after a low blow and an eye poke, in A-Train's EWWF singles debut.

matches.stipulation: EWWF Tag Team Championship tournament, round one
matches.finish: Dunsk broke a fishbowl over his own head to frame Ian Blade, and Sanders and Dunsk won by disqualification.
Homeless Joe Boxcar ran in and chaired Dunsk in the mouth, and Sanders and Dunsk won again by disqualification.
Sanders' acquaintance Diablos ambushed Ragnarok on the outside and Sanders followed with a low blow and a pin on Hazmat.
Krumm and Syko advanced quickly, Syko pinning Dunsk with the Syko Spin.
Winston pulled Syko off a near-fall at the last second and Paine covered for the pin.
Winston hit the Hangover on Rocky Camarelli for the pin.
Barry chokeslammed Winston over the top rope and Rheaume covered him for the pin.

matches.stipulation: tournament final; the vacant EWWF Tag Team Championship
matches.finish: Tao hit the Flow on David Rheaume for the pin, crowning Tao and Zen the tournament winners and the first EWWF Tag Team Champions.
After a ladder-assisted powerbomb through a table by Ash on both other men, Kain recovered to hit the Partycrasher DVD on Ash for the pin, retaining the title.
Tao hit the Flow on Syko for the pin, the champions retaining the same night they won the belts.

matches.stipulation: Masters Cell (steel cage, four tables and four chairs)
matches.finish: After both men traded near-falls and a mid-match respect angle, Demola hit his own version of a Tiger Bomb, driving Kontani onto a steel chair, for the pin.

matches.stipulation: EWWF United States Championship, four-way elimination
matches.finish: Adam Mitchell ruled the match would continue after a Love pin on the floor (no falls count anywhere), then had Tyler Darden help him beat down Love; Slade turned on Mitchell and Darden and let Love pin him clean in the ring.

matches.stipulation: EWWF Championship, three-way C-4 exploding match
matches.finish: After run-ins from Tom Collins, Smoove and Nick Demola on various sides and eight recorded explosions, Adam Mitchell entered the ring and personally counted the pin after draping Solkoff over Underwood; Solkoff retained.

notes: Six-part pay-per-view. The advance card's own “Sex Championship” listing for Ashlyn Summers vs. Homeless Joe Boxcar is staged and won on the belt the card's own text twice calls the Surrender Extreme Championship in the same breath (“she holds the Surrender Extreme Title...the SEX title”) — filed as one title, not two. Bronson Johnson (billed for the Cruiserweight match) never appeared; no match resulted.

name: EWWF Surrender, 2 October 2002

date.source: the fed's own text (“live on October 2, 2002”)

matches.finish: Syko hit Slade with a fireball and a chair shot from ringside; Camarelli rolled him up for the pin.
Love pinned Thomas with the Loveplex Version 2.0 while pulling the tights.
After Liam Zen's interference was carried off by three men described as the New Apocalypse's own, Tao rolled Ragnarok up with a handful of tights for the pin.
Kain turned an attempted chokeslam into a Jujigatame armbar for the tap-out.
Syko won by Fisherman Suplex with a bridge; Delaney then chair-attacked Syko and the returning Jimmy Slade after the bell.
Paulison reversed a Matthews rollup attempt into a German suplex with a bridge for the pin.
Hellkid hit a Tornado DDT (“Amazing Grace”) for the pin in a match both men fought hard.
Harvester of Sorrow and Axel Reed attacked both competitors and the referee; Winston fell on the prone Summers for the pin once the referee was slapped awake.

matches.stipulation: EWWF Championship, handicap match (Solkoff's own scheduled partner AsH never arrived)
matches.finish: Adam Mitchell entered the ring himself and fast-counted the pin after Despair piledrove Solkoff.

notes: A 16-man in-house tournament, run entirely on the EWWF's own broadcasts, for a belt the promotion's own commentary and ring introductions call the “SEWF World Championship” / “SEWF Heavyweight Championship” — the same name and lineage words the historical, closed SEWF used for its own world title, but never once treated in this text as staged, sanctioned or run by that promotion; the EWWF runs, judges and crowns it on its own shows, with only in-fiction references (Adam Mitchell's own SEWF presidency, the SEWF's own belt shown in flashback) tying it to that legacy. Filed as the EWWF's own distinct title, flagged for review. Jimmy Slade's ambush by Ryan Sanders and Tyler Darden on Andrew Krumm is shown only in a video insert of an unheld off-panel attack and is not filed as an appearance for Krumm.

name: EWWF Surrender, 10 October 2002

matches.finish: Kain hit the Partycrasher DVD for the pin, advancing to the final four; Axel Reed chaired both men afterward.

matches.stipulation: SEWF Championship tournament, quarter-final; EWWF United States Championship
matches.finish: Love pinned Paulison with the Loveplex Version 2.0 after fouling the referee with the Fair-Weather Johnson, but the referee ruled the bout for Paulison by disqualification — the fall the card's own stipulation tied to the United States Championship.
Hellkid rolled Camarelli up with a handful of tights for the pin.
Reed shoved the referee down and was disqualified, then chaired Archer afterward.

“Devilman” Christian Alicea, revealed as Ashlyn Summers' earlier kidnapper, chaired Rosa unconscious with a barbed-wire shot after both men and Axel Reed had already brawled through the ringside weapons; the referee's ten-count went unanswered.

Interference from A-Train and Liam Zen, plus a video insert of Ryan Sanders and Tyler Darden threatening the hospitalized Andrew Krumm, cost Syko three separate near-falls; Tao hit the Flow for the pin.

matches.stipulation: EWWF Championship; special referee Derek Irvin
matches.finish: Despair made Underwood submit to the Human Torment; special referee Derek Irvin rang the bell and credited himself with the stoppage.

notes: Tommy Kain, Sammy Paulison, Hellkid and Rune Tao advance to the SEWF tournament's final four (booked, off-panel, for the unheld “To Hell and Back”). The card's own text has Randy Love billed the reigning United States Champion with no document in this packet showing how he took it from Jimmy Slade after 8 August; recorded as a further honest gap. Ryan Delaney's ambush of David Rheaume and their scheduled match are shown as a real backstage fight with no bell, no decision and no formal result, so no match row is filed for it. The broadcast ends on Adam Mitchell shown bound, bloodied and unconscious in his own shower with Simon Solkoff's logo taped to the wall — an angle only.

name: EWWF Surrender, 5 December 2002

matches.stipulation: debut tag match, the Seventh Seal vs. the Chain Gang
matches.finish: Kosygin hit his own Ultimate Victory (Ace Crusher) on Garza for the pin, in both teams' debut.
With the referee repeatedly knocked out and Nick Demola personally pulling him from the ring, the Seventh Seal ran in and helped Delaney pin Camarelli, taking the EWWF Tag Team Championship.
Ragnarok nearly choked Spikowski out with the Louisville Slugger reversed, but a botched boot let Spikowski roll him up (Fair-Weather Johnson) for the pin.

matches.stipulation: SEWF Championship (Simon Underwood pulled from the scheduled triple threat)
matches.finish: Slade removed Simon Underwood from the match himself before the bell; Kain rolled Slade up with his foot on the ropes for the pin.

matches.stipulation: number-one contenders triple threat, no title
matches.finish: Cepacelli and Archer both had an arm draped over Winston when the three-count landed; the referee could not rule a winner and the new EWWF President ordered both Cepacelli and Archer into a title shot the following week.

matches.stipulation: EWWF Championship, three-way; special referee “Devilman” Christian Alicea
matches.finish: With Simon Solkoff ejected mid-match and Hellkid interfering throughout, Harvester of Sorrow jammed a table splinter into Ashlyn Summers' eye while Despair held his own ankle lock on Harvester; special referee “Devilman” Christian Alicea ruled Summers submitted first to an offensive move and awarded Harvester of Sorrow the title.

notes: Final held broadcast in this packet. Adam Mitchell has left the promotion between 10 October and this show (an unnamed, unseen figure is shown taking over as EWWF President); neither is served or minted as a change of the promotion's own registry row, since no document in this packet names the new figure. Simon Underwood's storyline exit (a scripted fall from the rafters at an unnamed hooded figure's command) is an angle carrying no match result. Both Extreme/Sex and World Championships are held by Harvester of Sorrow at the close of this broadcast — the Extreme/Sex title itself does not change hands on this card.
